market_summary: Tuesday close: Nasdaq -1.5%, S&P 500 -0.5%, Dow +0.85% to a record above 50,000, SOX -7.9% as chips unwound Monday's Huang-return rally. Money rotated into healthcare, consumer and value names. The 10-year held near 4.92%; Dec 9 Fed hike odds were last read about 91% (mid-Nov). Australian October CPI jumped to 4.9% y/y, trimmed mean 3.8%, putting an RBA hike on Dec 8 in play. GPU rents and DRAM spot held flat, so the selloff is in equities, not compute pricing.

headlines: SOX -7.9% Tue close as chips unwound Monday's rally: MU -11%, MRVL -9%, NVDA -6%, TSM -4%.
Watchlist hardware hit hardest: ALAB -14%, SKHY -10%, AMD -9%; CoreWeave -12%.
Compute pricing steady: H100 rent $3.10/hr, DDR5 spot flat. Selloff is equities, not demand.
AU October CPI 4.9% y/y, trimmed mean 3.8%: RBA Dec 8 hike now a live risk.
US GDP and PCE Wed 8:30am ET = Thu 12:30am AEDT; Deere reports Thu morning AEDT.
